name: Handwritten Annotations
visualIdentity: Handwritten lettering, underlines, arrows, circles, and simple diagrams with slightly uneven marker edges. Keep ink and accent colors restricted; point to the subject before showing each note and leave time to read.
suitableUses: Explicitly suits markup over screenshots or documents and annotations on charts, line art, products, anatomy, or mechanisms. Good for explanatory videos and interactive diagram or chart walkthroughs. These uses are inferred from the stated combinations.
limitations: Needs a subject to annotate. Avoid overcrowding, obscuring values, handwritten paragraphs, wobble on data marks, invented chart claims, or color fills in paired line art. Use narrative chapter patterns only when meaningful progression serves the explanation; omit transitions that obscure causality or break continuity.
palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: background #FFFDF7, foreground #233346, annotation accent #B54A3E; three discrete colors, no gradients. These are not canonical: preserve task, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors and their roles. Keep accents subordinate except for annotations. Suggested opaque text pairs meet 4.5:1, but recheck actual compositing and readability.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal SVG strokes with stroke-dashoffset or DrawSVGPlugin; sequence arrows, circles, and notes with the explanation. Point first, then introduce text, and hold for reading. Rough.js may make geometry sketch-like but does not create handwriting or authentic media; use suitable fonts or approved lettering assets. For video, drive deterministic state from seekable composition time. For HTML, annotations may toggle via buttons or appear on focus/hover with keyboard access. Scroll chapter/story patterns are optional and must preserve readable states and coherent backward seeks.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, vocals, or silence for the subject, audience, and brief; no audio assets are specified. Honor supplied choices, synchronize with picture, and preserve intelligibility.
assetRequirements: Requires a visible subject, such as a screenshot, document, chart, or illustration, plus readable font or lettering assets for notes. SVG paths suit scalable strokes and diagrams; tldraw is optional for authoring editable artwork. No specific source assets are mandated.
combinations: Pair with style-097 clean charts: reserve #B54A3E for annotations, keep chart marks #233346 on #FFFDF7, and explain one insight per state. Pair with style-027 contour line art: uniform-weight subject lines and uneven marker notes; land arrows before text. These pairings are explicit recommendations.
productionApproach: Choose style renderer and motion engine by fidelity; SVG/HTML-CSS draw, GSAP DrawSVGPlugin can reveal strokes, and optional tldraw/Rough.js support authoring or sketch geometry. HyperFrames is the video pipeline default; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, recording why. Pipelines handle assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export, not style rendering. For interactive HTML, bind controls and scroll to deterministic states; no specific HTML framework is mandated.
